response.sql: WITH filtered AS (SELECT sf.zoneref, s.entrystat, sf.traitcount FROM scanfeatures sf JOIN sites s ON sf.zoneref = s.zoneregistry WHERE sf.traitcount >= 489), grouped AS (SELECT zoneref, entrystat, AVG(traitcount) AS avg_traitcount, COUNT(*) AS record_count FROM filtered GROUP BY zoneref, entrystat), total AS (SELECT COUNT(*) AS total_count FROM filtered) SELECT g.zoneref AS site_code, g.entrystat AS access_status, g.avg_traitcount, g.record_count, CAST(g.record_count AS REAL) / t.total_count AS record_fraction FROM grouped g CROSS JOIN total t WHERE t.total_count > 0 ORDER BY record_fraction DESC NULLS LAST LIMIT 10;

assumptions.assumption: The inner JOIN drops scanfeatures rows with no matching site, and the traitcount >= 489 filter is applied before grouping, so the total record count is the number of joined, filtered records across all groups.
The fraction is a plain proportion (record_count / total), not multiplied by 100, and it is computed as a non-integer division (CAST to REAL) with no rounding.
Sites with a NULL entrystat form their own group, since GROUP BY keeps NULL as a group. NULLS LAST is used for the sort, which needs SQLite 3.30+ or PostgreSQL. The dialect was not specified.
Ties in record_fraction have no specified order, so the top 10 cut may include any of tied rows.
